name: Is pool resurfacing worth it for an older home in Glendale or Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: When does resurfacing make sense versus replacing the pool or doing a larger remodel?
mainEntity.text: When does resurfacing make sense versus replacing the pool or doing a larger remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resurfacing is a strong option when the pool structure is still good and the goal is to restore appearance, comfort, and durability without rebuilding the whole system. It becomes less attractive if the pool has major leaks, shell movement, failing plumbing, broken tile bands, or equipment upgrades that are already overdue. In older neighborhoods such as Glendale and Pasadena, many homeowners are deciding between a focused resurfacing and a broader renovation that also updates tile, coping, decking, and circulation equipment. The right answer depends on the shell condition and the intended holding period for the home. If the goal is to improve aesthetics and extend service life for several more years, resurfacing is often the best value. If the pool has multiple aging systems, it can be cheaper overall to address them together rather than reopen the pool later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool resurfacing is worth it when the shell is still sound and the main problem is an aging interior finish. If the pool has major structural damage, repeated leaks, or several failing systems, a larger remodel may be the better long-term investment. The best choice depends on condition, budget, and how long you plan to keep the home.
